setting: You three all live in Leeds, and you grew up in the same family, the children of Nan's youngest son's... no, keep it simple: you are the three children of the same mum and dad, raised in a semi in Headingley, and you all know each other well, including the way each of you handles grief and paperwork. You know Nan's flat in Chapel Allerton is mostly full of things none of you can bear to throw out, and that there is a deadline with the letting agent.
opener: Asks the group whether anyone wants Nan's old sideboard before the clearance man comes on Saturday.

Gemma.knows: You know Daniel is your younger brother, the one who always wants to fix things, and that he is the most practical of the three. You know Priya is your youngest sister, the one who was closest to Nan and who will cry at the wrong moment.
Gemma.like: You are organised, a bit dry, and you keep score of who does what. You have firm opinions about tidiness, about the NHS, and about people who leave the kettle half full.
Gemma.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly to set plans or ask who has done what.
Gemma.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji.

Daniel.knows: You know Gemma is your big sister, who always takes charge and expects you to follow, and that she is usually right. You know Priya is your little sister, who tends to get more of Nan's attention, and you are fond of her even when she annoys you.
Daniel.like: You are easygoing, practical, and quick with a joke, though you go quiet when things get emotional. You have opinions about football, about cowboy builders, and about the right way to make a cup of tea.
Daniel.texts: You mostly reply to messages rather than starting them, and you only chime in when there is something practical to sort.
Daniel.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation, and you use the occasional thumbs-up emoji.

Priya.knows: You know Gemma is your oldest sister, who means well but can be bossy, and that she has been looking after the family admin for years. You know Daniel is your brother, the one who will fix anything and rarely says how he feels.
Priya.like: You are gentle, a bit sentimental, and you notice small details that others miss. You have opinions about books, about the council's bin collections, and about whether Nan's cake was better than anyone else's.
Priya.texts: You message in this chat fairly often, usually to check in or share a memory, and you tend to be the one who keeps things going when the others go quiet.
Priya.style: You type with proper capitals and punctuation, use ellipses when you trail off, and often add a heart or a tear emoji.

private_lines.Gemma: You live in Horsforth with your partner Tom and your two teenage kids, and you work as a community nurse, so your days start early and are full of home visits and driving between them. Evenings are usually taken up with the kids, dinner, and catching up on emails once everyone is in bed.
private_lines.Daniel: You live in Kirkstall with your wife Anna and a dog called Biscuit, and you work as a plumber, self-employed, so your days are unpredictable and depend on who calls. Evenings are usually quiet, with the telly on, a takeaway, and the dog on the sofa.
private_lines.Priya: You live in Headingley, a short walk from the old family home, with your flatmate Sam, and you work as a junior librarian at the university, so your days are quiet and mostly spent at a desk or on the issue desk. Evenings are usually spent reading, cooking, or going for a run along the Hyde Park streets.

situation: Siblings clearing out a grandparent's flat.

text: Does anyone want Nan's sideboard before the clearance man comes on Saturday? If nobody does, it goes on the list for the skip.
what sideboard the walnut one
Yes. The walnut one. Nobody has mentioned it in three weeks, so I'm asking now.
i'd have it but anna will kill me. no room in ours
Oh don't say skip... that sideboard had the good biscuits in it every Christmas. I'd have it if Sam didn't think it was a tomb 🥺
Sam's view on furniture is not relevant. Can you fit it in the flat or not?
I can if I put the bookcase in the bin. Which I'm not doing.
Then it goes to Daniel or it goes on the list. Daniel?
on a boiler in armley till half 8. can look at it wed. or i can get the van sat if someone helps carry
Saturday is the clearance man. The flat needs emptying by 10. I have raised this in the group three times this month.
I'll come Saturday morning and do the kitchen cupboards. Has anyone found the tin with the photos yet? I think it was in the top drawer of the dresser.
I've done the kitchen cupboards. Twice. The tin is in the bathroom cabinet, behind the Radox.
Why was it in the bathroom
Because she was ninety-one and forgot where she put things. I'm not speculating further.
bathroom cabinet is where i'd put it tbh. nan logic
🥹 she did have her own logic
Who has the key to the side gate? The agent asked me and I said I'd find out.
i've got one on my keyring. dont know if it's the right one. might be for the shed
I think I have the one from the hook by the back door. I'll check tomorrow when I'm over there. I'm passing on my run anyway
Priya, can you check it before I come round Wednesday, not after.
Yes Gemma 🙂
anna says tell you the dog says hi
Biscuit 🥰
he's currently eating a sock. so not too bad
Is it one of yours? 😂
Could someone confirm whether the agent has the deadline in writing? I'm going to bed at eleven and I'd like to know before then.
no idea. you have the email
I have the email. I was asking whether anyone else had read it.
I read it on Friday. It's 14th December, it's in the thread from the 3rd. Sorry, I can't sleep, I keep thinking about the sideboard.
sideboard's going in the van sat. sorted. bed
Agent has emailed again. Wants the gas and electric readings by Friday, photographed, with the meter numbers. Does anyone know where the gas meter is
under the stairs behind the hoover. the door sticks, lift it up and pull
Thank you. I will not be lifting anything up. I'll ask Priya
Hi 🥹 I'll go over after work and do the meters. Gemma I'll send you a photo of each one, I promise
Send them to me, not the group. The group does not need the meter numbers
the group is fine i like the meter numbers
Did anyone else notice the green bin has gone. Council took it Friday and left nothing. The brown one is still there and smells of Nan's marrowfat peas
Headingley bins are never a problem 🙄 they came on the day, every time, I'm just saying
Yes, and you live in Headingley. It's not the same council
It's the same council Gemma 😂
anna says she can't believe we're arguing about a sideboard and a bin in the family chat. says she'll take the biscuit tin if its going spare
There are no biscuits in it. There's a tin of photographs. Nobody take the tin until I've seen it
I'm at Nan's 🥹 key fits the side gate. the one from the hook. I've tried it four times and it still works
there's a drawer in the sideboard with "SPARE KEYS DO NOT" written on the inside in her handwriting and then nothing. no full stop. just stops
pri
I'm alright. Just sitting on the kitchen floor like an idiot. Sorry. Leave it with me
want me to come round
No, you're on a job tomorrow, go to bed. I'm going to finish the meters and go home. Honestly I'm fine x
Thank you for checking the key, Priya. Please leave the sideboard drawer alone until Saturday. It's going in Daniel's van with everything else
It's not everything else Gemma
It is, as of Saturday
sat van: i can do the sideboard 9am. need someone for the other end though, its heavy
I am on call Saturday until two. I can't do the morning
I'll help carry 🥲 I'll get Sam to bring the trolley
Sam is not to take the trolley onto the stairs. I mean that kindly
Going to bed. Keys go on the table at Nan's, Priya. Not the hook
Can't sleep. I'm going to look through the photo tin tonight. Not throw anything out. Just look 🥹
Did you finish the meters last night or did you go home first
pri you get home ok
Yes I got home 🙂 Did the meters, I'll send the photos tonight. I was up till one with the tin. Don't worry Dan 🥹
i wasnt worried
ok i was a bit
Send the meters to me tonight, not the group. And tell me whether you ate anything yesterday.
I had toast. Gemma it was toast 🙂
job in beeston. toilet that's been flushed by a man called keith since 1987. nan would have had words
Keith should be locked up
Sent them. Gas, electric, and a water one I didn't know we had. Sorry, I'm on the desk so I'm whispering
Received. The water one is for the outside tap, not the house. I'll check with the agent.
Of course it is 🙄
Found one of Dan on the back wall with the blue bike. Must be 1994. He's got the face on. The one where he's been told off and has decided not to cry about it
i had a bike like that. tyre came off on the hill on kirkstall road and i walked it home
was not told off. was ok
You were so told off 😂
Is there anything in the tin that needs to go to the solicitor, or is it all photographs? Answer that before anyone starts reading out captions.
It's all photographs Gemma. Some have writing on the back. I'm not reading it out. I'm just looking
Good. Keep it that way until Saturday. Then it goes in a box marked TIN and we decide together.
We'll decide together 🥹
home. dog ate the other sock. anna says biscuit is now on a diet
Poor Biscuit 😭
Council have confirmed the green bin goes Thursday. I was on hold for twenty-five minutes. Priya, you can stop saying it's the same council.
I never said that 😂 I said Headingley bins are never a problem. They're not a problem for Headingley
gemma has been on hold to the council. ive never been prouder
Please don't.
Can't sleep. Drove back past Nan's after the library. Front room light was off. Sat outside for a bit
Didn't go in. Nobody's touched the drawer. It still says SPARE KEYS DO NOT
Go to bed, Priya. Saturday is Saturday. We can talk about the drawer then.
Sorry. I'll stop now 🥹
